backlog.title: Harden BUG-001 oversize-delete safety — close the note-write-failure data-loss window
backlog.description: BUG-001 (delete_created_files irreversibly deletes pre-existing files exceeding revert.maxFileBytes) was already fixed in commit ec5ad32 via a `spare` Set built from the oversize record in both backends' restore delete step, with passing integration + unit tests. HOWEVER, research uncovered a genuine HIGH-severity residual gap in the SAME bug class: the GitBackend persists oversize paths as a best-effort git note (try/catch-swallowed at git.ts ~418-432); if that note write fails, restore reads no note, the spare Set is empty, and `git ls-files --others` lists the oversize file (never staged -> untracked) -> it is unlinked (irreversible data loss). The fix's trust signal ('did the note arrive?') is itself best-effort, so trusting its ABSENCE to mean 'no oversize files existed' is unsafe. This phase closes that window with a defense-in-depth restore-time maxFileBytes size guard that is independent of the note round-trip. See plan/009_1ecb4b3cb372/bugfix/001_c5105b89490f/architecture/system_context.md (premise mismatch + code refs) and residual_risk_analysis.md (R1 mechanism + fix direction).

milestones.title: Defense-in-depth restore-time maxFileBytes size guard (both backends) + regression coverage
milestones.description: Add an independent, deterministic size check to the restore delete step in BOTH backends: any delete-candidate whose current byte size exceeds cfg.revert.maxFileBytes is spared (skip unlink) regardless of whether the oversize note/manifest round-trip succeeded. This is fail-SAFE — when the note is absent we cannot distinguish a pre-existing oversize file from a span-created large file, so the only safe action is to NOT delete (a leftover span-created file is recoverable via manual rm; a deleted pre-existing file is not). GitBackend needs a new `stat` DI seam (mirroring the existing `unlink` seam); CasBackend already receives `st` positionally from walkTree (it currently drops the third param — just accept it). Includes the key regression test: note-add failure + deleteCreatedFiles:true must NOT unlink an oversize file. NOTE: do NOT re-implement the existing spare Set (git.ts:869 / cas.ts:1119) — it stays; the size guard is additive belt-and-suspenders that runs AFTER the spare.has(rel) check.

tasks.title: Restore-time maxFileBytes size guard in the restore delete step (both backends)
tasks.description: Implement the defense-in-depth size guard in GitBackend (needs a `stat` DI seam) and CasBackend (st already passed by walkTree). Each subtask implies its own failing test (TDD): write the failing test -> implement the guard -> pass. The git subtask's implied test is the note-write-failure regression — the linchpin scenario that proves the guard closes the data-loss window independent of the note.

subtasks.title: GitBackend: add `stat` DI seam + maxFileBytes size guard in restore() delete step (closes the note-write-failure data-loss window)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/009_1ecb4b3cb372/bugfix/001_c5105b89490f/architecture/system_context.md (§ Residual HIGH-Severity Gap) + residual_risk_analysis.md (§ R1, § Fix Direction — GitBackend). The primary BUG-001 spare-Set fix ALREADY EXISTS at src/snapshot/git.ts:869 (`const spare = new Set(result.skipped)`) + :887 (`if (spare.has(rel)) continue`) — DO NOT re-implement it; the size guard is ADDITIVE and runs immediately AFTER that `spare.has(rel)` check. The gap: the note write at capture (git.ts ~418-432) is best-effort (try/catch-swallowed); if it fails, restore reads no note (git.ts ~811-824) -> result.skipped is [] -> spare Set empty -> `git ls-files --others` lists the oversize file -> unlinked (data loss).
2. INPUT: (a) cfg.revert.maxFileBytes (number; src/config.ts:108 field, :210 default 262144) available as this.cfg.maxFileBytes inside restore(). (b) the delete-candidate loop over `git ls-files --others` output in restore() step (c) (git.ts ~880-905): each iteration yields `rel` (POSIX workspace-relative path) + `abs` (resolveSafeWorkspacePath(this.repoRoot, rel)). (c) the existing GitBackendDeps interface (src/snapshot/git.ts:104-122) with optional `exec`/`scan`/`unlink`, constructed at ~272 (`this.unlink = deps?.unlink ?? fsUnlink`).
3. LOGIC: (a) Add `stat?: (path: string) => Promise<{ size: number }>` to GitBackendDeps (alongside unlink, ~line 117-122). Import `stat as fsStat` from node:fs/promises at the top (alongside the existing fsUnlink/fsRm imports at ~line 8-9). Store `this.stat = deps?.stat ?? fsStat` in the constructor (~272). (b) In restore() step (c) delete loop, IMMEDIATELY AFTER `if (spare.has(rel)) continue;` (git.ts:887), insert a best-effort size guard: `try { const st = await this.stat(abs); if (st.size > this.cfg.maxFileBytes) { if (!result.skipped.includes(rel)) result.skipped.push(rel); continue; } } catch { /* ENOENT/inaccessible -> size unknown -> fall through to normal unlink attempt (its own try/catch handles ENOENT) */ }`. This spares any delete-candidate whose current size exceeds the cap REGARDLESS of the note, and surfaces it in result.skipped (deduped) so the agent sees the incomplete revert. (c) TDD-implied test (test/git.test.ts, the KEY regression — this is the linchpin): construct a GitBackend via a helper that injects BOTH a recording unlink fake AND a stat fake (extend makeBackendWithUnlink at test/git.test.ts ~100-109, or construct GitBackend directly). Config: allowDeleteCreatedFiles:true, maxFileBytes:256. Fake exec: throwOn:{cmd:'notes'} (so BOTH capture note-add AND restore note-show fail -> note never persisted -> result.skipped empty -> spare Set empty), stdoutByCmd:{ 'ls-files': 'big.bin\nnew.ts\n' }. Stat fake: returns {size:1000} for big.bin (>256), {size:10} for new.ts. restore('BEFORE1',{revertFileChanges:false,deleteCreatedFiles:true}). Assert: result.deleted === ['new.ts']; result.deleted does NOT contain 'big.bin'; result.skipped contains 'big.bin'; unlinked array has new.ts but NOT big.bin. WITHOUT the guard this test FAILS (big.bin unlinked because empty spare Set); WITH the guard it PASSES. Also verify existing tests still pass: existing delete tests use fake paths (/fake/cwd/...) with the production-default stat -> ENOENT -> swallowed -> existing unlink behavior unchanged (NO existing test should need modification; if makeBackend/makeBackendWithUnlink gain an optional stat param, default it to undefined so the production fsStat is used). Mock: the fake exec (makeExec, test/git.test.ts ~66) + recording unlink + injected stat fake; no real filesystem needed for the unit test.
4. OUTPUT: GitBackendDeps gains an optional `stat` field (backward-compatible — production omits it -> real fsStat). restore() delete step now spares oversize files even when the note is absent, closing R1. RestoreResult.skipped surfaces spared paths for agent visibility. Consumed in place by the rewind tool's success text (no interface change).
5. DOCS: none — internal implementation detail of the restore delete step; no user-facing behavior, config surface, CLI flag, env var, public API, or exported type changes (GitBackendDeps.stat is an optional internal DI seam, not a public config). The changeset-level README safety-guarantee sync is handled by P1.M1.T2.S1 (Mode B).

subtasks.title: CasBackend: accept the walkTree `st` param + add maxFileBytes size guard in restore() delete step (belt-and-suspenders)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/009_1ecb4b3cb372/bugfix/001_c5105b89490f/architecture/system_context.md (§ Why CAS is immune) + residual_risk_analysis.md (§ Fix Direction — CasBackend). CAS is ALREADY IMMUNE to the note-write-failure window: its manifest write (cas.ts ~546-560) is the LAST step before `return label`; if it fails, capture returns null -> no ref to restore from -> delete step never runs (no orphan ref). So this guard is PURE belt-and-suspenders for uniformity with the GitBackend — it costs one signature tweak + one line and makes both backends share the same deterministic safety floor. The existing spare Set at cas.ts:1119 (`const spare = new Set(manifest.skipped ?? [])`) + :1125 (`if (spare.has(rel)) return`) STAYS; the size guard runs AFTER it. KEY DETAIL: walkTree (cas.ts:411-440) already calls `this.fs.stat(abs)` and passes the result as the THIRD positional argument to the `visit` callback, whose type is `(rel, abs, st: {size, mtimeMs})`. The restore delete-step callback at cas.ts:1123 currently declares `async (rel, abs) =>` (drops `st`) — so the size is already computed and available, just not accepted.
2. INPUT: the restore() delete step's walkTree callback (src/snapshot/cas.ts:1123) — change its signature from `async (rel, abs) =>` to `async (rel, abs, st) =>` to accept the already-passed stat object. cfg.revert.maxFileBytes available as this.cfg.maxFileBytes.
3. LOGIC: In restore() step (c), inside the walkTree callback, IMMEDIATELY AFTER `if (spare.has(rel)) return;` (cas.ts:1125), insert: `if (st.size > this.cfg.maxFileBytes) return; // SPARE — defense-in-depth, independent of manifest`. This mirrors the GitBackend guard. (b) TDD-implied test (test/cas.test.ts or test/integration/revert-cas.test.ts): an oversize pre-existing file (> maxFileBytes) + deleteCreatedFiles:true + allowDeleteCreatedFiles:true must SURVIVE even if somehow absent from manifest.skipped (force the belt-and-suspenders path). For the unit layer (test/cas.test.ts, CasFs fake makeStateFs), configure the fake stat to return a size > maxFileBytes for the target file and OMIT it from manifest.skipped, then assert it is NOT in result.deleted and unlink was not called for it. The existing F-revert-delete-oversize integration test (test/integration/revert-cas.test.ts:750) must still PASS (the file is in manifest.skipped -> spared by the spare Set before the size guard; no behavior change). Mock: CasFs fake (makeStateFs/makeStateBackend) for unit; real filesystem for integration.
4. OUTPUT: CasBackend restore() delete step shares the same deterministic maxFileBytes safety floor as GitBackend. No interface change (the walkTree visit type already includes st).
5. DOCS: none — internal implementation detail; no user-facing/config/API/exported-type change. Changeset-level README sync handled by P1.M1.T2.S1 (Mode B).
